cells.date: Śaka 1003, Mina, Kṛish-pa-pañoha-ml, Sunday. Śakn 1034, Uttarāyana.
cells.remarks: Records the grant by the king, of the village Khonna to three hundred learned Brahmans.

Gives the genealogy of the Ganga kings and the lengths of their reigns down to Anantavarman and mentions that his coronation was celebrated on Saturday, śukla-pakshatritīyā, Revatī, in the month Kumbhu of the Śaka year 999, states that since Mundaparu which had been originally granted to brahmans along with the village of Khonna in the Varshavardhani-vishaya by the king's grandmother, Janakadēvī in the Śaka 1003 was subsequently reunited with the village of Gara, eighty-eight vrittis of land were taken over in return for it from the village of Talupu and granted by the king to the brahmans as compensation.

Gives the usual genealogy of the Eastern Chalukyas down to king Vijayāditya. Registers the grant, in the presence of the assembly of Mahājanas, free of all taxes and imposts, to the Vedic scholar Pampanārya-Bhaṭṭopādhyāya of the Parāśara-gotra for the merit, prosperity and health of the king. The donee and his ancestors are praised for their scholarship. The inscription was composed by the poet Mutteya-Bhaṭṭa and inscribed on the plates by Paṭṭala. The grant is addressed to the Kuṭumbis (householders) of Gudda-vāj-vishaya.

Gives the usual genealogy of the Eastern Chalukyas sovereigns down to the king. Registers the grant, by the king, of the village Krunūru, free of all taxes and imposts to the Vedic scholar Pampanārya of the Parāśara-gotra, who was a resident of the village of Pasudova. 'The donee's scholarship is highly praised. The inscription was composed by the poet Muttiya-Bhaṭṭa and inscribed by the Paṭṭalaka. The grant is addressed to the Kuṭumbis (householders) of the Gudda-vāj-vishaya.

Records the grant of the village Ballavolu, otherwise called Tiruvēhkaṭapura, situated in the Padanāgu-mahāstma, a subdivision of the Chandragiri-rajja to the scholar Tirumalachārya, who was the eldest son of Appayāchārya and grandeon of Siṅgarachārya and who belonged to the Bharadvaja-gōtra. The grant was made by the king at the instance of his younger brother Vēnkaṭapati.

Records the grant of the village Kivvalār, otherwise called Vēṇpalāmbasamudra and situated in the Maṅgalār-naṇu, a subdivision of the Chandragiri rajja, as sarvamāṇya for the expenses of teeding the Vaishṇavas when the images of the god Ādikēśava and of Embermānār (Ramannja) were taken in procession to the garden established by Vēṇpalāmba, the queen of Tirumalaraja, at Sriperumbu[d]ār and for paying the wages of keepers of this garden.

cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Tirumāni-kuppa, otherwise called Chinnatimma-rajanapuru, in the Chandragiri-rajja, by the king, to the Vedio scholar Purushōtama-Bhatṭa, of the Gautama-gōtra and Āśvalayanna-sūtra, made at the request of the minister Ramaraja on behalf of Āraviṭi Timmaraja and Chinna-Timmaraja.

cells.remarks: Registers the grant by the king, of (twenty-two villages in Gadagina-dēśa (i.e. Gadag country) which comprised 66 villages and which was situated in Toragallu-nādu in Lakkumdēya-vēnthe, a subdivision of Pomja-Hastināvati (i.e., Hampi) to the gods Tryambaka and Viranarayana at Gadag at the instant of Vaptvilasa Śri-Kriyasakti-guru. The control and management of the two temples was visited in Sammanapabarya who was a brahmah of the Kasyapa-gōtra and Bodhayana-sūtra and who was the sēnulōgu (accounts officer) of the Gadag-dēśa.

The entire management of the charity was left in charge of the Pandārasannidhi of Tiruvāva-dūturai. Mentions Kaṭṭi|rava] Narasaraja-Uḍaiyar as the ancestor of the king.

cells.place: On the walls of the Gāyatrī temple
cells.remarks: Stones out of order and some lost. Begins with the introduction pularam-pōla etc. Seems to register a remission granted by the Mahāsabhā of Valuvolur on some temple lands, in return for money received by them from a certain individual in the temple of Urupirāvar-Uḍaiyār and Ayapperuñjēlivyār. On the same stone in another line is a damaged and incomplete inscription which records a grant of land as compensation by a certain Akalankarayar for the money given to his wife as strīdhanam by her father Anapayarayar but which he had spent away.

cells.location: Kōmal
cells.place: On the south wall of the Sundarēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Registers a tax-free grant of land at Tattamangalam on the northern bank of Virasōlappēruātu in Tirruvalundur-nādu, a subdivision of Jayankonḍaśōla-valanādu, to the temple of Ayangāri-Uḍaiyār alias Uḍaiyār-Nāyanār by mēl alus Kulatungasōlāchaturvēdimangalam for the maintenance of a matha.

cells.location: Kōmal †
cells.place: On the north wall of the Sundarēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a tax-free gift of land by several persons to a certain Hanasthagavar belonging to Bhaṇītikshanyaparishat for the maintenance of a matha.

cells.location: Kōmal †
cells.place: On the north wall of the Sundarēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives a list of lands acquired as tirumuttakkēni for the temple of Alagiya-Nāyanār on the north side of Tiruvālappērunallur at Tattamangalam a brāhmadeyya in Tiruvalundūr-nāḍu. Mentions Tellichchēri, a brāhmadēyu in Kuyumbōr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Uyyakkondar-valanādu.

cells.location: Kōmal †
cells.place: At the entrance into the shrine of the goddess in the Kripākshēśvara temple in the same village (as Sundarēśvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to register a gift of land by purchase by a certain Kalappalarayar for feeding 20 brāhmaṇas daily in a śālai (feeding house) attached to the temple of Tiruvāvpūdi-Ālvar (Krishņa) at Gangaikonḍaśōla-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Elumagalur
cells.place: On a stone lying in a field
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to register a sarvamānya gift of land for offerings in the temple of Meykānēśvara temple. Not far from this stone are two others in a field which contain an imputation against violating the charity.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the north wall of the Gokhurēvara temple
cells.remarks: Registers a gift by the king, of 6 mā of waste land brought under cultivation for the maintenance of two gardeners looking after a flower-garden belonging to the temple of Tirukkolambam-uđaiya-Mahādēva called Rajadbi-rajan-tirunandavanam after the king. Jayaṅgondaśoĵa-Uttaramantri figures as a signatory.

cells.location: Elumagalur †
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.date: 15th year, Karka-ṭaka, ba. dvādaśī, Mēḍay, Magai-yatti (Mṛigaśīrsha). [date-calculation appendix, No. 46: [15th] year, Karkaṭaka, ba. dvādaśī, Monday, Magaiyatti = A.D. 1182, July 11, Monday ; ·73. The nak. was Mrigaśirā which was current till ·57 on Monday.]
cells.remarks: Beginning of lines built in. Commences with the introduction LMPIVND etc. Registers a sale of tax-free land to the temple of Tirukkolambam-udaiya-Mahadēva in Tiraimūr-nādu, a subdivision of Uyyakkopāravalanādu by the big assembly of Alaziyaśola-chaturvēsi-maṅgalam, for the money received by them out of the amount deposited with the temple by a resident of Tiravadutarai, for feeding the pilgrims to the temple. Mentions the temple of Angivinnagar-Ālāvar where the assembly held its deliberations.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land as tiruchchennāḍippuram to the goddess of Madhurāntaka-Uṇā-Bhaṭṭārakar in the tem-ple of Tiruvāḍuturai, by Ponnambalakkūttan alias Vikrama-Chōḷa, the queen of Uttama-Chōḷa, after purchasing the same from a certain Kaḍay Siṅgam through her son Mahāmātran Gautaman Śrīkaṇṭhan of Śatta-nūr, a brāhmaḍēya in Tiraimūr-nāḍu on the southern bank. The land was made tax-free by the assembly of Pēravūr in return for a certain amount. Mentions the coin Iḷakkarkuśu as equivalent to 1/5 kāśu-pon.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Records the order of the king to the trustees (sthānattār) and the dēvadānamis to bring under cultivation 6 mē of waste-land for the maintenance of two gardeners looking after the temple garden called Hajadirāj-tirunandavanam. This is the preliminary of the transaction mentioned in No. 45 above.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Seems to register a kaiyōṭu (pledge) of some land given to the temple by a certain person of Mana-bu[sh]aṇa-Vinayaka-ḷḷu-Piḷḷaiyār situated in the street round the temple, by a private individual for the money received by him. Above this is a fragmentary inscription of about the same period recording a sale of land.

cells.location: Elumagalur †
cells.place: On the north and west walls of Kripākshēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a sale of land made tax-free to the temple at Tirukkoḷambam in Pēravūr-nāḍu by the assembly of Tirukkoḷambam, a brāhmaḍēya in the same nāḍu. Men-tions the temple called Urkkayach-Chemmaiyūr.

cells.location: Elumagalur †
cells.place: On the same walls
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction [Tirumagal pōla] etc. Registers an agreement made by the Sthānattār and two Uruchchar (musicians) of the temple to perform certain ceremonials on every moon-day to the god Nāṇḍōṭya-Vāḷaikkar out of the interest on the money and the produce on the land received by them from a certain officer of the Sirudanam Perundaram numot Maraiṅkāḍan Dēvan alias Rājarāja-Taḍigaipāḍi-Naḍalvān of Sattanūr.

cells.location: Elumagalur †
cells.place: On the west and south walls of Kripākshēśvara temple. †
cells.date: 33rd year, Mina, 6u. pañohadaśi, Thursday, Uttiram. [date-calculation appendix, No. 52: Rājakēsarivarman alias Rājādhirājadēva. 33rd year, Mīna, śu. pañchadasi, Thursday, Uttiram = A.D. 1051, February 28, Thursday; ‘44; ‘70.]
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Śiva-Bārapā-Śrī etc. Records the agreement made by the big assembly of Abay-śrava-chaturvēdimaṅgalam, a brāhmadēya in Tirainurnādu, a subdivision of Uyyakkondār-valaṇadu to pay all the taxes on certain specified lands belonging to the temple in lieu of the interest on 260 kāsu received by it from the temple. Mentions the grain-measure Āyiravaṇ-marakkāl and a ehannel called Kuñjaramallaṇ-vāykkāl.

cells.location: Elumagalur †
cells.place: On the south wall of Kripākshēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a tax-free gift of land by the assembly of Davēdi-mangalam, a brahmādēya in Pēravūr-nāḍu, in return for 14 kāśu received by it.

cells.location: Elumagalur †
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a provision made for the offer-ing of piṇḍamūḍu to the god by a resident of Virudarāja-bhayaṅkarapuram in Takkalūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of A[rum]oḷidēva-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Damaged and incomplete. Records a gift of gold for some ornaments to the image of Kutta-[Na]yakar [Nataraja] in the temple by a devotee.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records an agreement by two Brahmans of the temple to burn a perpetual lamp before the god, for which the money was paid in made by a resident of Iḷunkā-kuḍi in Pēravūr-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Records another agreement by the same persons for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple for money received by them from a private individual (name lost). Mentions the coin dramma.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.date: 6th year, Makara, 6u. Friday, ohaturdaśi, Hasta. [date-calculation appendix, No. 58: 6th year, Makara, éu. Friday, chaturdasi, Hasta. Su. chaturdaéi and nak. Hasta cannot combine in the month of Makara. ‘The intended date was probably A.D. 1840, January 14, Friday. Sua. 14 ended at °59 and the nak. was Puinarvasn (not Hasta) which was current till -32 of the day.]
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land for worship to the temple of Tirukkōṭṭiyūr-uḍaiya-nāyanār by a certain individual for the merit of his deceased father.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Ends of lines built in. Begins with the introduction ௵கோப்பரகேசரி வர்மரான etc. of Rājēndra-Chōḷa I. Records an agreement by the Śiva-Brāhmaṇas to burn a perpetual lamp in the temple for the money they had received for the purpose.

cells.location: Tirukkolambiyur
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a similar agreement made by two Brahmans to burn a twilight lamp in the temple.

cells.location: Elumagalur †
cells.place: On the east wall of the maṇṭapa in front of Kripākshēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction ௵பூமகள் வளர etc. Registers the royal order making over 10 vēli of land as dēvadāna for offerings to the god Tirukkoḷambam-uḍaiya-Mahādēva. Mentions the throne called 'Vāṇādhirājan' in the palace at Muḍigoṇḍachōḷapuram.

cells.location: Elumagalur †
cells.place: On the wall of Kripākshēśvara †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land as dēvadāna to the temple of the bar on behalf of Mahā-Gaṇapati-Nayiṇār the karapikkam of the king.

cells.location: Koṭṭaṅguḍi
cells.place: On the south wall of the Kōṭīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Stones displaced and some lost. Seems to register the provisions made to the god by a gift of land free of taxes to the temple.

cells.location: Pēravūr
cells.place: On the north wall of the Ādityēśvara temple
cells.date: 18th year, Kanya, śu. dvitīya, Wed-nesday, Śittirai.
cells.remarks: Registers a sale of land at Anapayanalūr to the temple of Tiruvāḍuturai-Uḍaiyār at Pēravūr in Pēravūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-vaḷanāḍu by a certain Rājarāja-Vaitarayan, the headman of Maṅgalam in Ikkaṭṭu-koṭṭam, a subdivision of Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-maṇḍa-lam, on behalf of his wife Palliyalvi who inherited the land from her father, but could not cultivate it herself and pay the taxes due thereon.

cells.location: Pēravūr †
cells.place: On the north wall of the Ādityēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land to the temple by the same lady.

cells.location: Pēravūr †
cells.place: On the south wall of the Ādityēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives an inventory with details of their weights, of the gold ornaments and vessels as found in the treasury of the temple in the 26th year of the king. The characters seem to be of the twelfth century A.D.

cells.location: Pēravūr †
cells.place: On the south wall of the Ādityēśvara temple. †
cells.date: 16th year, ‘Siṅha, śu. chaturthī, Wednesday, Sōti. [date-calculation appendix, No. 67: 16th year, Siṁha, śu. chaturthi, Wednesday, Sōdi = A.D. 1194, August 21, Sunday ; ·79; f.d.n. ·47. The week-day quoted in the inscription is evidently a mistake for Sunday.]
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land for the maintenance of a perpetual lamp in the temple of Tiruvāḍuturai-Uḍaiyār at Pēravūr in Pēravūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Jayangoṇḍachōḷa-vaḷanāḍu by a native of Arkaṭṭu-kuṟṟam in Nittavinōda-vaḷanāḍu. He had bought the land originally in auction (Kulōttuṅga-śōḷan-peruvilai).

cells.location: Pēravūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the Ādityēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land free of taxes, for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple, by a certain Tiruppēr Śri-Kṣishna-Bhaṭṣa Somayaṇi. Peravur is mentioned as a hamlet of Suttamalli-ohaturvēdimaṅgalam.

cells.location: Pēravūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the Ādityēśvara temple. †
cells.date: 13th year, Makara, śu. dvādaśī, Tues-day, Mṛigaśīrsha.
cells.remarks: Portions lost in the middle and last line built in. Begins with the introduction प्रमब्बमपि etc. Registers a similar gift of land and a lamp-stand for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple, by a certain Yaidumbaraya of Puttamvṅgulam in Tiruvār-kārgam in Geya-māgkka-valanaḍu. The land had been originally purchased by him in auction (Kulōttuṅga-sōlaṇ-peruvilai).

cells.location: Pēravūr †
cells.place: On stones built into the west wall of the Āiyanār temple in the same village (as Ādityēśvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Portions lost. Registers a sale of a house to the temple by a certain Baḷōndumani-Bhaṭṭa of Tiruvāḍuturai on behalf of his wife.

cells.location: Pēravūr †
cells.place: On stones built into the west wall of the Āiyanār temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Seems to register the gift of a house for the maintenance of a lamp in the temple.

cells.location: Maṇḍai
cells.place: At the entrance into the Abhirāmi-Amman shrine in the Sundarēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a provision made for the celebration of festivals on the Kathasaptami and the following ashṭami days every year in the temple at Tirumigaich[obūr] in Uyyakkondāśola-valanādu by Śevappa-Nayakkar-Ayyaṇ of Neđuṅguṇram for the merit of the king.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple
cells.date: 37th year, Kanya, śu. pañchami, Wednesday, Ani-lam.
cells.remarks: Registers the agreement made by the Śiva-Brāhmanas who had turns of service in the temple of Tirumadām-Udaiyar at Tiruvalundūr, a brahmadēya in Tiruvalundūr-nādu, a subdivision of Jayaḥkondāśola-valanādu to bring water daily from the river Kavērt for the sacred bath of the deity, in return for 1,450 kūśu received by them from two merchants of the village.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 5-1st year, Bibha, śu. tritiyā, Wednesday, Ādiraī. [date-calculation appendix, No. 74: 5 + 1st year, Simha, ba. tritiyā, Wednesday, Aśvatī = A.D. 1184, August 26, Sunday ; ·18; ·81. The week-day quoted in the inscription is evidently a mistake for Sunday.]
cells.remarks: Gives a list of men and women who were bound to the temple by service in perpetuity.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 23rd year, Kar-kaṭaka, śu. pañ-chamī, Monday, Aṭṭam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 75: Tribhuvanachakravartin Sōlakērajadéva 'who was pleased to take Madurai, Karuvūr, Īḷam and the crowned head of the Pāṇḍya.' 23rd year, Karkaṭaka, śu. pañchami, Monday, Attam = A.D. 1200, July 17, Monday ; f.d.t. ·23; f.d.n. ·44.]
cells.remarks: Records an agreement similar to that registered in No. 73 above made by the Śiva-Brāhmanas of the temple in return for the money received by them from a resident of the village called Kaviniyaṇ Vasudēvaṇ Vamana-Bhatṭaṇ.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives a list of the persons who had bound themselves to serve in the temple. The characters are of the 12th century A.D.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 17th year, Siṅha, ba. pañchamī, Wednesday, Rēvati. [date-calculation appendix, No. 77: 17th year, Simha, ba. pañchami, Wednesday, Rēvatī = A.D. 1162, August 1, Wednesday; f.d.t. ·17; ·76.]
cells.remarks: Records the agreement by the Śiva-Brāhmaṇas to burn a perpetual lamp in the temple for the interest on the amount they received from a certain person (name lost).

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 17th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 78: 37th year, Kanyā, śu. pañchami, Wednesday, Aṇilam = A.D. 1214, September 10, Wednesday ; ·81; ·04.]
cells.remarks: Registers a similar agreement by the Śiva-Brāhmaṇas to burn a perpetual lamp in the temple of Tiruvannāśram (Tiru-vagnīśvara)-Uḍaiyār for the interest on the amount they received from one Kaviṇiyan Vāmaṇa-Bhaṭṭan.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 30th year and [8]3rd day, and 24th year, Dhanus, ba. ohaturdaśi, Ani-lam, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 79: 24th year, Dhanus, ba. chaturdaśī, Aṇilam, Monday = A.D. 1203, December 8, Wednesday ; f.d.t. ·18; ·43. The week-day quoted in the inscription is probably a mistake for Wednesday.]
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land made in the 24th year of the king for maintaining a lamp in the temple by a certain Kaviṇiyan Vāṅgadēvan Vāmaṇa-Bhaṭṭan.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives a list of the lands added to the temple as tirumattak-kāṇi till the 20th year of the king. Records a sale as (Subhavēḷai) to the temple by the assembly of Tiruvāḷundūr, a brāhmaḍēya in Tiruvāḷundūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Vīra-Rājēndra-vaḷanāḍu, of land belonging to two individuals named Kaviṇiyan Śrīkaṇṭhan and Peri-yaṇḍār for 1,060 kāśu, in pursuance of the royal order confiscating the lands of those mischievous people who were a source of trouble the brahmans, Vēḷḷāḷas and to the temple. Mentions the (Vishnu) temple of Tiruk-kaḍavai-Āḷvār in the village.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 1[6]th year, Kaṭaka, ba. pratbamā, Monday, Aviṭṭam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 81: 2 [5]th year, Kaṭaka, ba. prathamā, Monday, Avittam = A.D. 1193, July 16, Friday ; ·97; f.d.n. ·37.]
cells.remarks: Registers a sale of 75 kuļi of land to the temple for 300 kāsu by a certain Upamanniyadėvap, a resident of the village.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 11th year, Kumbha, [śu]. chaturdaśī, Wednesday, Pu-śam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 82: 11th year, Kumbha, [śu]. chaturdaśī, Wednesday, Pūśam = A.D. 1189, February 1, Wednesday ; f.d.t. ·07; ·24.]
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a similar sale of 120 kuḻi of land to the temple for 360 kāśu by a certain Vachchhiyan Sūppiramaṇiyan-Bhaṭṭan.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a sale of 115 kuḻi of dry land for 690 kāśu to the temple by a certain lady through her husband Maḍilan Kumārasvāmi-Bhaṭṭan.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 11th year, Dhanus, ba. tritiya, Thursday, Pu-[ś]am. [date-calculation appendix, No. 84: 11th year, Dhanus, ba. tritiyā, Thursday, Pūśam = A.D. 1188, December 8, Thursday ; ·79; ·59.]
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a similar sale of 50 kuḻi of land for the temple for 250 kāśu by a certain [Vachchhiyan] Sūppiramaṇiyan Uyyakkonḍān-Bhaṭṭan.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 9th year, Kaṭaka, śu. dvādaśī, Monday, Mūla. [date-calculation appendix, No. 85: 9th year, Karkaṭaka, śu. dvādaśī, Monday, Mūla = A.D. 1186, June 30, Monday ; ·28; f.d.n. ·94.]
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a sale of 105 kuḻi of dry land for the temple for 210 kāśu by a certain Vachchhiyan Sūppiramaṇiya-Bhaṭṭan and his mother.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 9th year, Kaṭaka, śu. chaturdaśī, Monday, Mūla. [date-calculation appendix, No. 86: 9th year, Karkaṭaka, śu. chaturdaśī, Monday, Mūla. Details same as No. 85 above excepting the tithi chaturdaśī which is a mistake for dvādaśī.]
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a sale of 130 kuļi of dry land for 260 kāsu to the temple by a certain Vachobiyan Śuppiramanniyaṇ Adītta-Bhatṭaṇ.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 7th year, Mīna, śu. chaturthī, Thursday, Kārttigai. [date-calculation appendix, No. 87: Vīra-Rājēndra-Chōḷadēva. 7th year, Mīna, śu. chaturthi, Thursday, Kārttigai = A.D. 1070, March 18, Thursday; ‘87; ‘66.]
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a sale of 100 kuḻi of land to the temple for 200 kāśu by two persons named Maṇḍiyaviyan Śatti Tiruvāradamudaiyān and Maṇḍiyaviyan Śatti Vināyakaḍēvan.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 7th year, Mīna, chaturthī, Wednesday, Pu-śam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 88: 7th year, Kumbha, śu. chaturdaśī, Wednesday, Pūśam = A.D. 1070, January 27, Wednesday; f.d.t. ‘26; ‘72.]
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Registers a sale of 98 kuļi of dry land for 196 kāsu to the temple by a certain Kaviniyaṇ Narayanaṇ Alaiñjakolari-Bhatṭaṇ.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On the right door-jamb of the entrance into the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged at the end. Registers an agreement by four Śiva-Brāhmaṇas of the temple of Tirumudan-udaiya-Mahādēva to burn two twilight lamps in the temple for the money they had received from one Kaṇiyan Kaḷayan Ejuvāḍi-yaṇār of the village.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On the left door-jamb of the entrance into the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers another agreement made by the same Śiva-Brāmanas to burn 6 twilight lamps in the temple for the money received by them from various people at different times, from the 32nd year of the king.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On a pillar in the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Has only a portion of the introduction commencing with the words Ellalaksar Ellala etc. Registers a gift of 160 sheep for burning a perpetual lamp and for the supply of ghee in the month of Sittirai to the image of Sri-Krishna 'who was pleased to stand' in the Ohitramandapa of the teople of Tirukkadavudaiya-Emberuman at Tiruvalundur, by a servant of the king named Valikketaupai Gunasilan of Mulikkurumbu in Uraiyur-körram, and his wife Aiyadi Pattagai. Below this is a fragmentary inscription of the same period which records a gift of 45 sheep by a lady for a lamp.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On a second pillar in the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of gold for the supply of ghee from its interest to the temple on the days of amāvāya, by a certain Tūppil Chattikumāro-Bhattian residing at Viranārāyanachohēri, a quarter of Viranārāyanach-chaturvēdi-maṅgulam on the northern bank.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On a third pillar in the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a smile of 7 mā of land, free of taxes, to the temple of Sri-Krishna by the big assembly of Tiruvalundur for 15 kāsu received by them from Valikketaupai Gunasilan, mentioned in No. 91 above, who is also stated to have set up the image of the goddess in the temple.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On a fourth pillar in the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers the remission of taxes by the big assembly of Tiruvalundur, on the land given for the maintenance of a flower-garden to the temple by Kaṇṇan Mālai alias Uḍaiyār-kūttan of the temple of Tiruvālīśvaram in the Ambar-nāḍu.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On a fifth pillar in the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Has only a portion of the introduction commencing with the words திருமா வளர etc. Registers a sale made by the assembly of Tiruvalundur for the supply of a kuruni of ghee for offerings to the image of Tirukkadavudaiya-Emberuman Nayanar-devar on the day of Punarpūsam every month, with the interest on the money received by it from the person mentioned in No. 91 above. Lower down the pillar is another inscription of the same king which however stops in the middle of the introduction.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On a sixth pillar in the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. Has a portion of the introduction commencing with the words Ellalaksar Ellala etc. Records a grant of land for the maintenance of two persons singing the hymne (tiruppudigam) during the three services in the temple of Tirukkadavudaiya-Dēvar.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On the west wall of the mandapa in front of the central shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records an agreement by the sthānatār of the temple of Tiramadamudaiya-Nayānār to plant coconut trees in the street's belonging to the temple and to pay half the yield thereof to the temple. One of the streets is called Vikramaśolan-tiruvidi.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On a pillar in the Saundarya-Nayaki-Amman shrine in Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Srt we etc. Records a gift of 48 sheep for burning a half-lamp in the temple of Tiruvagniśvarattu-Mahadēva at Tiruvaļundar in Tiruvaļundūr-nađu a subdivision of Uyyakkondār-vaļanađu by a resident of Mupaippađi. Do. Gift of 45 sheep for burning a half-lamp in the temple by a certain Kumaray Palla[varai]yyan of Vaļugūr. Mentions a committee called Kāļi-gapattār.

cells.location: Kīḷaiyūr †
cells.place: On another pillar in the Saundarya-Nayaki-Amman shrine in the Vēdapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Do. Gift of 45 sheep for burning a half-lamp in the temple by a certain Kumaray Palla[varai]yyan of Vaļugūr. Mentions a committee called Kāļi-gapattār.

cells.location: Palaiya-Gudalur
cells.place: On a stone in the ruined Agastīśvara temple
cells.remarks: States that door-jamb, the flooring and the Śrī-pīṭham were the gifts of a certain Tiruvalamudaiyān.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Srt we etc. Records an agreement by the assembly of Ilachohikuđi alias Vikramaśiṅgach-chaturvēdimaṅgalam a brahmadēya in Manni-nađu a subdivision of Rajendrasithha-vaļanađu, to pay the taxes levied, in the land-survey made by order of the king, on the lands belonging to the temple of Tiruvāvađutrai-nđaiya-Paramasvami at Sāttaṇūr a brahmadēya in Liraimūr-nađu, in payment of the interest on the money which they had received some time previously from the temple but which they were unable to pay back. In continuation of this is another inscription of the 25th year of the king, recording a gift of land by the residente (ūrōm) of Ilaṅgarikuđi in Pērāvūr-nađu a subdivision of Uyyakkondār-vaļanađu, for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.date: 6th year, Mithuna, Su., Saptami, Uttiram. [date-calculation appendix, No. 102: Parakēsarivarman alias Rājēndra-Chōḷadēva. 6th year, Mithuna, śu., Sunday, saptami, Uttiram = A.D. 1018, June 22, Sunday. The nakshatra ‘Uttiram’ quoted in the inscription is evidently a mistake for ‘Hasta’, which was current till ‘81 on Sunday. śu. saptami ended at ‘65 of the day.]
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction திருமா வளர etc. Registers a sale of land to the temple, made tax-free, by the assembly of Abhayāśrayach-chaturvēdimangalam alias Sattanūr, a brahmadeya in Tiruvalundur-nāḍu, a subdivision of Uyyakkondār-vaḷanāḍu. Mentions the hall called Ulagalandān to the north of the temple, where the assembly met and made the sale. The land is in the 5th year of the king by the residents (ūrōm) of Kīlūr in Pāṇḍi-nāḍu for burning a perpetual lamp before the god.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the same introduction. Records a gift of land, made tax-free for 200 hiśas received from the temple, by the assembly of Mērkīlimaṅgalam in Tiruvaļundar-nađu, a division of Uyyakkondār-vaļanađu with the condition that the Māhēśvaras of Sarvadēvan-tirumēdam, called after the king's guru, should be fed daily. Mentions a maid-servant of the palace (periyavēlam) called Taduvaṇ Arumoļi.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives a list of the gold and silver vessels and ornaments and also images of some deities, presented to the temple on various occasions by several persons including the Abhimānatōṅgar, the mother of Trailōkya-mahādēviyār, and the mother of Rājēndra-Chōjadēva, and by the preceptor (guru-sēvar) of Rājādhirāja and the servants of the palace (periyavēḷam).

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction [திருமகள் போல] etc. Incomplete. Registers the agreement made by the assembly of Siṅganallūr a brahmadēya in Tiruvaḷan-dūr-nāḍu on the southern bank, undertaking to pay the taxes on the lands belonging to the temple in lieu of the money due to the temple by certain individual and which had been confiscated by Rājarāja-Mahārāja (Rājarāja I) under circumstances the details of which are lost in the inscription.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: The inscription is engraved by the side of two figures one standing behind the other facing a liṅga. States that the front figure is that of Āḷavaiy Saṅdirādittan of Vāraṇappāl who constructed a tier (படை) of the temple and the other, of Nakkaṉ Vaṇṇattāḍi a maid servant of the palace (periyavēḷam).

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers the boundary limit (of the end ? pur) purchased by the assembly of Sirupuliyūr by the residents (ஊர்) of Kaḷrnalūr in Pārāvūr-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers the royal confirmation of the grant, made by the Mahādēvar, of certain privileges in the temple to Pāra-śurāma Saṅkaran of Iḷaṅkāruḍi for his acts of piety such as the provision for offerings and worship to the god at Tiruvāḍuturai on the festival days in the month of Puraṭṭāśi, the construction of the temple called Madhura-kāntavinnagar, and the gift of village making endowments for offerings and lamps therein, and for the provision made by his father for the maintenance of a perpetual lamp in the temple at Tiruvāḍuturai.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Beginning of lines built in. Commences with the introduction [திருமகள் போல] etc. Registers a sale of a set of land to the temple for 40 kāśu by the assembly of Pērāvūr a brahmadēya in a subdivision of Uyyakkoṇḍār-vaḷanāḍu with an agreement to pay all the taxes for a further sum of 90 kāśu received by the assembly.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Beginning of lines built in. Seams to register a tax-free gift of 4 ½ eēli of land to the temple by the irrigation committee (?) (entyttaii kūlaiyaraiyargal) of the assembly of Sirāpaichohūr who had got it tax-free from Parakēsarivarman alise Karikala-Choladeva who raised the banks of the (river) Kavēri (Kāvērikaraikonđa).

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land by a certain Tayandādan of Vīramangudi, after purchasing it tax-free from the assemblies of Sirupuliyūr, and Siranāichchōlūr, for the maintenance of two hymners, two gardeners and two maid-servants for gathering flowers for garlands, for offerings in the temple and for singing the hymns during the service. The donor's descendants (the Śivayōgiyar and the Āchāryas) are to serve for seven festival days beginning with the asterism Mūla.

cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a sale of land house-site for 20 kāśu by the assembly of Palaiya-Vanavanmādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam in Innamlar-nāḍu a subdivision of Rājēndra-piṇḍa-vaḷanāḍu, to Ālvār Śrī-Parantakan Śrī-Kandavai-Piraṭṭiyār who endowed it on Śavaṇan Arulāḷan alias Chōḷa-Uttama-Chōḷa-Achāryan and his descendants as the physician of the village. It was engraved on the temple walls by the order of the king.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Engraved in continuation of the previous inscription. Records the agreement made by the assembly mentioned above to pay the taxes on the same land in return for 80 kāśu received by it from the donor.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land as Sudamakkāni (?) to Tirukka Kadiyavan Appi Vēduday by the āchāryas of the temple.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.date: 4th year, Mēsha, śu. navami, Tuesday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 115: Kulōttunga-Chōḷadēva I. 4th year, Mēsha, śu. navamī, Tuesday = A.D. 1074, April 8, Tuesday; ‘73. The nak. was Āślēsha which was current till ‘48 on Tuesday.]
cells.remarks: Fragment. Mentions a matha and the village Sutta-mali-chaturvēdimangalam in Iravūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Rājēndar-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift, by a native of Tiruvijimilalai a brahmadṭya in Veṇpāđu in Uyyakkondar-valaṇađu, of paddy from the interest on which the Siva-brāhmayus of the temple agreed to get daily three pots of water from the river Kavēri for the sacred bath during the three services of the god.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Gives a list of the different metallic images of the deities with their measurements, and lamp-stands in the temple of Tiruvavadeturai-Udaiyar in Śat'aṇur alias Abaya-śraya-obaturvēdimangalam.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers an agreement made by the Siva-brāhmayas to a certain Śatkaraṇ Īsaṇ of Kuttaṇur in Nallarūr-nađu to burn a perpetual lamp in the temple for the 30 kāsu received from him, and to a certain Āttiraiyan Kottađi Vasudēvaṇ of Vadavār who had made a gift of 8 kāsu to provide for a pot of water from the Kavēri for the sacred bath of the god during the mid-day service.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Begins with the introduction [Tamil script] etc. Registers a similar agreement made by the Śiva-brāhmaṇas of the temple to burn two perpetual lamps in the temple and to get daily three pots of water from the river for the sacred bath of the god during the mid-day service.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.date: 9th year, Tulā, Saturday, Tiruvōṇam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 120: Rājakēsarivarman alias Rājaśājadēva (I). 8th year, Tulā, Saturday, Tiruvōṇam. Probably A.D. 994, October 13, Saturday; f.d.n. ‘95. On this day which was in the śukla-paksha shashthi ended at ‘18 and then śu. saptami commenced.]
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of land as nṛityabhōga on behalf of the temple, by the assembly of Śāttaṉūr that assembled in the hall called 'Chatuśālai', to a certain Kumaraṉ Śikaṇḍaṉ who had the Śākkai-kāṇi of the village, for acting the seven aṅkas of the Āryakkūttu on the festival day in the temple of Tiruvāvaḍuturai-Āḻvār in the month of Puraṭṭāśi.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the west and south walls of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in. Begins with the introduction [Tamil script] etc. Seems to record an agreement by the assemblies of Śāttaṉūr in Tiraimūr-nāḍu and Śiṟṟāṉaichchūr in Tiruveḷundūr-nāḍu to pay the taxes on the temple lands situated in their villages in lieu of the interest on the amount due from them to the temple which they were unable to pay.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Registers a sale of land to the temple of Tiruvāvaḍuturaidēvar by the assembly of Śiṟṟāṉaichchūr for the money paid on behalf of the temple by a certain Tirukkaṟṟaḷip-Pichchaṉ.

cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 99 sheep by a certain Nanban Vireśvaran for maintaining a perpetual lamp in the temple.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Gift of gold for burning a perpetual lamp in the temple by a merchant of Karuppūr in Tiraimūr-nāḍu on the southern bank.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Records a remission of taxes on the land purchased for the temple by a certain Kāḍaṉ Śāttaṉ of Neṟkuppai in Tañjāvūr-kūṟṟam, by the assembly of Śiṟṟāṉaichchūr for the money received from the donor. This land and another purchased for the temple from the same assembly by Tirukkaṟṟaḷip-Pichchaṉ (mentioned in No. 122 above) were to be utilised for the maintenance of servants who blew the conch and horn, held the parasol and looked after the flower-garden.

cells.place: On the same wall ..
cells.remarks: Registers the purchase of 11 mā of land for the maintenance of the pipers serving in the temple, from a resident of Śiṟṟāṉaichchūr by Tirukkaṟṟaḷip-Pichchaṉ who is stated to have built the temple (at Tiruvāvaḍuturai). The assembly of the village made it tax-free on receipt of 16½ kaḻañju of gold.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Ends of lines built in. Registers a sale of tax-free land to the assembly of Sāttanūr for 15 kaḻañju of gold which had been given to the temple for the sacred bath of the god on the day of Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti by a certain Ōmāśi Oṉṉuṟān Kuṭṭan of Tiruvāṇaikkā, a arcaṉa-brāhmaṇa in Kiḷiyūr-nāḍu.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction tirumanni valara etc. Registers a sale of land, made tax-free, to the temple by the assembly of Kīḻūr, a brahmādēya in Tiruvalundūr-nāḍu received by it.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the same introduction. Records a gift of 96 sheep for a perpetual lamp in the temple by a devotee named Vēmbān Śaṅkaran alias Tillaiyāḻagappa-Piḷḷai. Records also the appointment of a certain Taṟumūḍu-śēkhara-Paṇḍitar for the daily mid-day service of Gōmuk-īśvara and (his consort) Aṭuḷakkuha-Nāyaki.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: States that (the figure of) Ilaiya Tirunāvakkaraiyar the devotee of Karralip-Piraṉār (god). The inscription is engraved by the side of a standing figure in a worshipping attitude, with hands placed close to the chest in the front. The inscription is engraved near this (figure) in front of a linga, with hands placed close to the chest in the worshipping attitude. States that (the figure of) Śil-Karralip-Pichchar.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: The inscription is engraved below a standing figure worshipping a linga in front. The name is given as Tiruvīśūr ḍiār alias Tirunāvakkaraiyan, the devotee of Śil-Karralip-Pichchar.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction tirumanni valara etc. Registers the agreement made by the Śiva-brāhmaṇas to provide offerings to the god for the mid-day service and feed an aparai daily with the same, out of the interest on 40 kāśu received by them from a certain Nārāyaṇan Tiruvāykkulamuḍaiyāṉ in Oma-nāḍu, a sub-division of Jayangoṇḍa-śōḻa-maṇḍalam.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Built in the middle. Registers a sale of land, free of taxes, by the assembly of Sāttanūr to Śaṅkaran Oṟṟi, a member of the Ādittapuram-tiruvā-kkīḻār-kōyil, for the maintenance of a cocoanut and a flower-garden for the sacred bath in the middle. Registers a similar sale of land by the same assembly for the maintenance of three perpetual lamps in the temple and for a flower-garden.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. Seems to record a royal order confirming the sale of a woman to the temple. Mentions Poḷḷyaṉ Paḷḷavaraiyar the royal secretary.

cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †

cells.remarks: States that the śikhara (of the central shrine) was the gift of a certain Pallava-Mahārāyar (a member of the order) of Kānkēsavatār.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the east wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land in Sirrālaichchūr by Kāyalip- Plohahu of Tiruvavadutturai who allotted the same among the hymners, those bringing water for the sacred bath of the god and the pipers in the temple.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai †
cells.place: On the east wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers the provision made by Karraip-Pichchar and the dēvakaṛmis of the temple for meeting the expenses of offerings to the deity on all the saṅkrānti days and for special bath on the two Ayana-saṁkrānti days by purchase of 3 ma of land for 8 kasu obtained as shares from a certain Kānkēsapuliyūr-Nakkan of Ta[t]tākadambūr in Kār-nādu on the northern bank.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the east wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: The inscription is engraved by the side of a standing figure worshipping a liṅga in front. The name is given as Daman Analan alias Namasivāyan of Sirradi in Tirunariyūr-nādu.

cells.location: Tiruvāduturai
cells.place: On the east wall of the central shrine in the Gōmuktiśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a remission of taxes on the lands belonging to the temple both by gift and purchase, by the assembly of Sirrālaichchur for the money received by it from Tirukkarraipp-Pichchar.

cells.remarks: Unfinished. Begins with the same introduction. Records a tax-free gift of 1,000 kuḻi of land to the temple by a number of persons, for the maintenance of a feeding house (aruchchalai) attached to the temple.

cells.remarks: Begins with the same introduction. cells.remarks: Registers a remission of taxes on 6 ma of land given to the temple after purchase, by the assembly of Āyayastrāyachaturvēdimaṅgalam for the maintenance of the maṭha called Nār-patteṇṇāyiravan-maṭham in return for 37 kaḻañju received by it from a certain lady.

Begins with the introduction STMLCKSS L L L etc. Records the gift of 10 cēli of land (by the king) for the maintenance of (a feeding house called) 'Arumoñdēvan' and for the daily offerings of havirbali to god Ādavallar in the temple, with the condition that the tax on half the portion was to be paid by the temple, and that on the other half by the assembly of Talaichohahgāṣu. Also records another tax-free gift of 5 cēli by the assembly for an annual festival in the month of Śittirai and a remission of taxes on the land granted in the 17th year of the king for the havirbali-arehnu in the temple.

cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction STMLCKSS L L L etc. Records the decision of the assembly while holding its meeting in the Mummuñisōlan-maṇdapa, to pay the taxes in return for the 50 kāśu received by it, on 2 cēli of land at Pūdapūr in Vilai-nāṣu which had been purchased by the Periyatali-Mahadēvar temple in the southern quarter of the village, for meeting the expenses of the festivals in the month of Vaigaśi and of feeding the Brahmins on those occasions. It also agreed to pay the taxes on 2 cēli of temple land at Kilppulam in lieu of the interest on the 100 kalañju which had been received by it on promissary note (kaiyoṭuttōlai) from the same temple. These two transactions were engraved on the walls of Tirunannipalli-Ucdaiyar temple by the order of the assembly.

cells.date: 3rd year and 6th year, Āṇi, ba. 2, Friday, Tiruvōṇam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 193: Parakēsarivarman alias Rājēndradēva. 6th year, Āṇi, ba. 2, Friday, Tiruvōṇam = A.D. 1057, June 20, Friday; f.d.t. ‘83; f.d.n. ‘60.]
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Tirumagal maruviya etc. Records the agreement of the assembly to pay the taxes on certain lands in lieu of the interest on 80 kāśu received by it in part from the officer Irumuḍiśōḻa-Mūvēndavēḷār in the 36th year of Vijaya-Rājēndradēva ‘who died on the elephant back’ and in the 3rd year of Rājēndradēva. The produce from the lands was to be utilized for the midday service to the image of Tiruvaiḷambaram-uḍaiya Nāyanār, his consort and Piḷḷaiyār set up by the officer in the temple of Tiruvaiḷambaram-uḍaiyār in the village. Refers also to a gift of 3 kaḻañju for the lamp made on the day of ‘beating the kōchcharam’ (?) on the marriage day of Āḷavandār, made in the [3]rd year of Parakēsarivarman Rājen-dra-Chōḷadēva ‘who trod Parakkēśari, Gaṅgai and Kaḍāram.’

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On the west and south walls of the Chaṇḍēśvara shrine. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction Pūmaruviya tirumādum etc. Records an exchange in consideration of 200 kāśu received from the temple for 2½ vēḷi of free-land by the assembly of Taḷichchēri-kāḍu. The land is stated to have been given to the temple for the havirbali-archchanā to the god Tiruralaṅgāḷum-uḍaiya-Mahādēva in the village, but found unproductive owing to the high level of the land and the consequent difficulty of irrigation.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On the south wall of the Malaiyā-maṇḍai-Amman shrine in the Naṭṭupāl-śvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones out of order and portions of the inscription are lost. Seems to record a gift of money realized as taxes on certain shops, for worship and offerings to the image of Mūlaparaśai-Vindyakappallaiyār set up in the temple.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.dynasty: On slabs built into the east wall of the prakāra (outside) of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Tamil

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On a stone set up at the corner of the tank near the Naṭṭupāl-śvara temple. †
cells.dynasty: On a stone set up at the corner of the tank near the same temple.
cells.remarks: States that the water of the Poṟpiṟavāvi-tīrttam should not be utilised for irrigating any lands other than the flower garden of the temple of Naṟṟuṇaināḍar-Svāmi.

cells.dynasty: On stones built into the north and south walls of the Nanmadiya-Perumal temple at Talachchangadu (Talai-Udaiyavar-Koyilpattu).
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction [Tamil script] etc. of Rājarāja I. Stones out of order and portions lost. Records a gift of 100 kāśu by the assembly of Talaichchaṅgāḍu for feeding in the name of Rājarāja 10 Brahmins in the temple of Tiruchchitrakūḍattu-Āḻvār and for havirbali-archana to the god. Specifies the sources from which this 100 kāśu was to be raised.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On the north and west walls of the Nammālvār-Perumal temple at Talaichchangādu. †
cells.dynasty: On the north and west wall of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Portions lost. Records a gift of land to the temple of Śrīmadhurai-Ādivarāhadēvar at Talaichchaṅgāḍu by a resident of Iḍaiyāṟṟukkuḍi, a brahmadēya in Maruṅgal-nāḍu.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.dynasty: On the west wall of the same temple.
cells.date: Parakēsarivarman, 'who took the head of Vira-Paṇdya.'
cells.remarks: Portions lost. Records a gift of land to the temple of Śrīmadhurai-Ādivarāhadēvar at Talaichchaṅgāḍu by a resident of Iḍaiyāṟṟukkuḍi, a brahmadēya in Maruṅgal-nāḍu.

cells.place: On the north, west and south bases of the Nammālvār-Perumal temple at Talaichchangādu. †
cells.dynasty: On the north, west and south bases of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Stones built out of order and portions lost. Begins with the introduction [Tamil script] etc. of Rājēndra-Chōḷa I. Records the remission of taxes on certain temple lands by the assembly in lieu of the annual interest of 150 kaḻañju due on 400 kaḻañju of gold (by the standard Rājēndraśōḻan-māḍai) received by it from a merchant of the Vīraśōḻa-maḍigai at Gaṅgaikoṇḍaśōḻapuram on behalf of the temple of Tiruvayppāḍi-Āḻvār.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On a pillar set up on the north side of the central shrine in the Sankharanyēśvara temple in the same village (as Nammālvār-Perumal temple). †
cells.dynasty: On a pillar set up on the north side of the central shrine in the Śankharanyeśvara temple in the same village.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a silver vessel to the big temple of Mahādēva at Talaichchaṅgāḍu by Pirāntakan-Mādēvaḍigaḷ alias Sembiyan-Mahādēvi the mother of Uttama-Chōḷa. Above this are three lines of writing of the time of a certain Rājakēsarivarman.

cells.dynasty: On another pillar set up on the south side of the same shrine.
cells.remarks: The inscription is very badly worn out. Seems to belong to the early Chōḷa period. Records a sale of land by the assembly to the temple of Tiruveḷvikkuḍi-Mahādēva in the village.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On the north wall of the first prākāra of the Sankharanyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records an assignment, by the assembly of Jayangondachōla-nallūr to the three Siva temples of Rajēndra-Chōladēva-Udaiyār, Kuśaliśvaram-Udaiyār and Viliśvaram-Udaiyār of the piece of three vēli of cultivable land which had been lying unclaimed (parruhu), as their tax-free property, entering them as such in the alugu and pottagam (register), with the provision that if during the next land settlement it was marked as tirappu instead of irayili the inhabitants of the village should pay the taxes on the granted land.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On the north wall of the first prākāra of the Sankharanyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of 4 vēli of land by the big assembly for house-sites and maintenance of the temple of the [dēvada]na-houses who had to keep watch over the village and its eastern hamlet, as they had no quarters before and as the allowances they had been receiving were not enough for their maintenance. 'This land was to be inalienable under any circumstances except in case of treason.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On the west wall of the first prākāra of the Sankharanyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Do. .. Stones lost. Begins with the introduction பார்மாதமும் to. of Rajadhiraja II. Gives the list, with their situation and extent, of the dèvadâna lands of the big temple at Tulaichchaângadu in Åkkur-nâdu, a subdivision of Jayangondaśola-valanâdu as entered in the register. Mentiones a land called 'Ioṇmênjaśola-vilâgam'

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On the west wall of the first prākāra of the Sankharanyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the change of a vêli of dèvadâna land into tirund-mattukâñi owing to the failure of the tenant to pay the annual due of 8 k lam of paddy on the land successively and the consequent accumulation of rent for a number of years. The tenant's consent was obtained for the f.rfeiture and the land was let out on lease (அண்டிழதல் பழம்) to the tenants, with the sauction of the assembly.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāra of the Sankharanyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the order of the members of the assembly doing the gramakāryam of Talaichchāngādu from the month of Dhanus, defining certain obligations and privileges appertaining to the sthāna lands in the 10 kaffalai of the village and also in the surrounding hamlets.

cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record an order of the assembly abolishing certain rents which were being collected for paying the whole staff which was now annually appointed, instead of being permanent. It was to carry on its function with the paddy contributed among its members themselves.

cells.location: Kilaiyur
cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāra of the Sankharanyēśvara temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1396, Jaya, Makara, śu. dvitīyā, Monday, Aviṭṭam = A.D. 1475, January 9, Monday ; -52; -49. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 212]
cells.language: Saka 1396, Jaya, Makara, śu, dvitrya, Monday, Aviṭtam.
cells.remarks: Gift by a Brāhmaṇ of three vēli of land in Sōlāpāṇḍyanallūr a hamlet of Talaichchāngādu, for the maintenance of a service instituted by him in the temple of Peruntiruk-kōyiluḍaiya-Nāyanar.

cells.location: Kilaiyur †
cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāra of the Sankharanyēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers the renewal of the title deeds ( அனுப்பாகப்பத் முழுகு) through the village assembly, to all the residents who were in the enjoyment of lands in the several hamlets of the villages up to the 18th year (of the king), by Pillai Sendamangalam-Udaiyar Sivacavana-Perumal alias Irungolar, and Pillai Purośaikkudaiyar Sutyavakkar Tiruvēgaunbam-Udaiyar as the old registers (பொத்தகம்) and documents (காசம்) had been lost in the disturbed state of the country (தித்தகள்) in the 5th, 1[1]th and 16th years (of the king).

cells.location: Kilapperumballam
cells.place: On a slab lying near the Naganathēśvara temple
cells.remarks: States that Sottavalli[na]llur is the gift (to the temple) for a service in the name of king Srirangaraya.

cells.location: Melapperamballam
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Dakshinapurīśvara temple
cells.remarks: Built in the beginning. Seems to record a sale of land in mada-tree, by some private individuals of Maruchēri in Ākkūr-nādu to the temple of [Tiruva]lamburam-Udaiyār, to provide for worship and offerings to the images of Kuttādu[dēvar] and Tājāgappi-Nāchchiyār set up in the temple by a certain Vānavan-Kōchchayan.

cells.location: Melapperamballam †
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Dakshinapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a sale of 8 persons of Tiruvalamburam-Udaiyār in Ākkūr-nādu, a sub-division of Jayangondachōla-valanādu, by a certain Kavakāsi-Kuhaiyan Kumaran alias Tambirāntōlan of the same village.

cells.location: Melapperamballam
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Dakshinapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Do. Records a similar sale of 6 persons by a certain Soman Tattan of Nangūr alias Sripadadūli-chaturvēdimangalam in Rajadhiraja-valanađu, for 13 kāśu.

cells.location: Melapperamballam
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Dakshinapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Do. Records another sale of 7 persons including herself to the temple for 30 kāśu, by a lady called Araya; Perungađi with her hosband Sodi Tali alias Chandośvarap-Pēraiyar of Ambar as her agent (முதுகண்).

cells.location: Melapperamballam
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Dakshinapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Do. Records the sale to the same temple by a certain Nambanambi Kađuga!-Nangui, wife of a Velala residing in Solapandyanallur, a hamlet of Talaichohangađu, of 15 persons comprising herself, her daughter, grandson, his children and others for 30 kāśu.

cells.location: Melapperamballam
cells.place: On the north wall of the central shrine in the Dakshinapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 9th year, Kanya, su. daćam1, Monday, Pushya. [date-calculation appendix, No. 220: 9th year, Kanyā śu. daśamī, Monday, Pushya = A.D. 1126, September 13, Monday ; ·94; ·93. Śu. is evidently a mistake for ba., for śu. 10 and nak. Pushya cannot combine in the month of Kanyā.]
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction முமாதபேசை 1 eto. Records a sale of land and the remission of taxes on the same and some other land measuring in all about 3½ vēli, belonging to the temple of Tiruvalumburam-Udaiyar at Talaichohangađu in Ākkur-nađu, a sub-division of Rajanarayuna-valanađu, by the assembly (mahāśabhai) of Peruñjirainallār, a brahmadēya in Nangūr-nađu in Rajadhiraja-valanađu, in return for a lump payment of 40 kāśu by the temple.

cells.location: Melapperamballam †
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Dakshinapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land, free of taxes, for two flower-gardens measuring 18 mâ in extent, by the assembly (mûlavarâsai) of the village (Thahâchchênguḍu) in return for a payment in lump of 100 kâsu by the temple.

cells.location: Melapperamballam †
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Dakshinapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date: 8th year, Kurttigai, 6u. 12, Wednesday, Sadaiyam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 222: 6th year, Kārttigai, śu. 12, Wednesday, Śadayam. Śu. 12 and nak. Śadayam cannot combine in the month of Kārttigai.]
cells.remarks: Built into the right end begins with the introduction Svasti śrī, etc. Mégalam is a gift by purchase of land 2½ mâ of land, at Vêlapâdi, a subdivision of Aiyampâdi in Vêla-nādu, a sub-division of Kottam in Chola-valanâdu, for worship to the images of Katta-deva (Natarāja), his concert and Truppalliyaraip- Pîrthiyar set up by him in the temple. He also got the taxes on the land remitted by a cash payment of 70 kāsu, to the assembly (mûlaparushai) which held its sitting in the Hummu(li)tôṇ-Paramanîllam(hall).

cells.location: Melapperamballam
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Dakshinapurīśvara temple. †
cells.date:
[12]th year, Mithune, 6u.
tritiya, . . . . .
Pūsam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 223: [12]th year, Mithuna, śu. tritiyā,.......6·+; Pūśam. Probably A.D. 1174, June 4, Tuesday ; ·43; ·58. In the absence of the week-day, the date cannot be verified.]
cells.remarks: Do. Begins with the introduction கடல்சூழ்ந்த பாரமாதேவி etc. of Râjadhârāja II. Seems to record a tax-free gift by the same assembly of some lands to the temple for worship and offerings to the images of certain deities set up in the 8th year (of the king) by a native of Maiamlaip-Pa[l]aiyanur[ dû] in gondasôja-maṇḍalam.

cells.location: Akkur
cells.place: On the east wall of the first prākāra of the Tântônrîśvara temple
cells.remarks: Records the gifts of some plots of land by some private individuals for the maintenance of twilight lamps set up by them in the temple of Tiruttantōŋri-Madomôdaiyār at Akkur alias Râjêndrasinha-chaturvêdimangalam. provision being made for the irrigation of the lands granted.

cells.location: Akkur †
cells.place: On the west wall of the first prākāra of the Tântônrîśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Completely erased after the first two lines. Begins with the introduction கடல் சூழ்ந்த etc. Seems to record some transaction of the assembly (perunguri-makkal) of Akkur with the temple regarding [some rents in] paddy to be paid to them.

cells.location: Akkur †
cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāra of the Tântônrîśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Completely erased after the first two lines. Begins with the introduction கடல் சூழ்ந்த etc. Seems to record some transaction of the assembly (perunguri-makkal) of Akkur with the temple regarding [some rents in] paddy to be paid to them.

cells.location: Akkur †
cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāra of the Tântônrîśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged Records a gift of land for the various requirements of worship and offerings in the temple of Tiruttantôŋri-Mâdau-udaiyār at Akkur alias Râjêndrasinha-chaturvêdimangalam, by a certain Adalamandan. Suriyan alias Tillaimu-vâyiran while he was ailing from an acute disease, also providing for additional offerings after his demise.
