cells.location: Akkur †
cells.place: On the east side of the base of the mandapa in front of the Tântônrîśvara temple. †
cells.date: 18th year, Makara, su. pañchami, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 228: 18th year, Makara, śu. pañchami, Monday = A.D. 1233, January 17, Monday ; ·81. The nak. was Rēvatī which was current till ·87 on Monday.]
cells.remarks: Beginning of lines lain. Records the gift of portions of lands belonging to several private individuals for forming a road to take the image of the god to the (river) Kāvəri for the sacred bath in the mouth of the Vâigai. The plots thus acquired being entered in the accounts as tax-free, by the order of the assembly (kullapparru-makkal) who were paid from the treasury (kôyil) from the fund of Kûmaran-gôvindan alias Vîrkudai[y]an of ......

cells.location: Akkur †
cells.place: On the east side of the base of the mandapa in front of the Tântônrîśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the sale of land to Alagiyapallavan alias Virapatya during his pilgrmage to all the sacred places south of the Kâvəri, after his conquest of the Hoysalas (Pôśalar, and the Pāṇdyas.

cells.location: Akkur †
cells.place: On the west wall of the central shrine in the Vaikuntha-Nārāyana-Perumal temple in the same village (as Dakshinapurīśvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Records that this temple was built for the welfare of the King by Ulagāpyal[l]ai alias Vanadarayar of Kapparai residing in Niyyam, a subdivision of .... Kottam. The Sanskrit verse engraved below and stated to have been composed by Bhaṭṭa Narasim'ha and Bhaṭṭa Devarâdha respectively repeat the same information and refer to the donor as the king's minister.

cells.location: Akkur †
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Vaikuntha-Nārāyana-Perumal temple. †
cells.remarks: Records an order of the [kul]apparru-makkal who were in charge of the village (administration) of Akkur from the donor of the village (Alagiyapallavan) to the king of and the village, a tax-free fund for opening a road to the river Kâvəri, to carry the image of Rajarâja-Vinvagar[Em]perumâl for the sacred bath on festival occasions, as the temple authorities of Tiruttantōri-Madomudaiyār refused permission for the sacred bath of the deity as it was not customary according to that temple. Also registers another gift of land for the requirements of worship on those occasions.

cells.location: Tillaiyadi
cells.place: On the east wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Sarangapāṇīsvāmi temple
cells.date:
12th year, .....
pañchami, Visakha, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 232: 12th year,....... , pañchamī, Viśākha, Monday. Probably A.D. 1146, March 4, Monday ; f.d.t. ·08; ·53. The month and the paksha missing in the inscription would then be Mīna and bahula.]
cells.remarks: Built in at the right end. Begins with the introduction மண்டலமுடையாள் etc. Seems to record the sale of two vel'i of land made tax-free at Sättamangalam, to the temple of Vikramsôliśvaram-Udaiyār at Tillaiyalinallûr by six individuals for 16 kâsu. Mentions Gaigakoṇḍachôlapperunteru at the right end. The assembly met together. Built in at the right end. Records the merit of a certain mangalam to the same temple for the merit of a certain [R]āmappa-Nāyakkur.

cells.location: Tillaiyadi †
cells.place: On the east wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Sarangapāṇīsvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Beginning of lines Built in. Records the tax-free gift of one veli of land at Poraiyanur, a hamlet of Tiruvaiñjalikahi by the assembly of the village (mahâsabha) for the expenses and offerings to the image of the goddess in the temple.

cells.location: Tillaiyadi †
cells.place: On the north wall of the prākāra maṇḍapa.
cells.date: 24th year, Kumbha, su. trayodasi, Monday, Pūsam.
cells.remarks: Similar to Nos. 167, 184 and 226 above. The temple at Tillaiyavarn is included among those which were benefited by the king's munificence of 10,000 varâhaq.

cells.location: Tillaiyadi †
cells.place: On the south wall of the prākāra maṇḍapa. †
cells.remarks: Records the permission granted by the king at the request of Pallavarayar to a certain Rājarāja-Pichchan to make over the right of ‘tiruppaḍimāṟu’ in the temple of Tillaiyāli-īśvaram at Ambar-nāḍu, a sub-division of Jayangoṇḍaśōḻa-vaḷanāḍu, to persons of his own choice.

cells.location: Tillaiyadi †
cells.place: On the south wall of the Chōḻa-Vinayaka shrine in the Sarangapāṇīsvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Very much damaged. Seems to eulogize the deity, Mentions Ilaṅgār-Kōchchaṅgarimākoḍi.

cells.location: Tillaiyadi †
cells.place: On the west wall of the inner gōpura of the Sarangapāṇīsvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Records an agreement by the weavers residing in the streets round the temple to raise subscription among themselves at a kāśu on each working loom for renovation of the temple of the shrine of Vikrama-Iśvaramuḍaiya-Uḍaiyār, which had cracked in places.

cells.location: Tillaiyadi †
cells.place: On the west wall of the first prākāra of the Sarangapāṇīsvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 10 kāśu to the temple towards the charges for measuring a bīri and paḍakku of salt daily from the salt pan called Aḻiyūrai alias Rājēndraśōḻa-iśvaram granted (by the king) for meeting the expenses of offerings during the ardha-yāma service called Vikrama-śōḻan-śandi in the temple of Tillaiyāli-īśvaram-Uḍaiyār.

cells.location: Tillaiyadi †
cells.place: At the east entrance into the prākāra round the Bṛihannāyaki-Amman shrine in the Sarangapāṇīsvāmi temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the shrine for Periyannāyaki-Amman at Tillaiyāli by Nelai Rama-Nayakkār (mentioned in No. 233 above) who also provided for the ardha-yāma service to be conducted therein.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Built in in the middle. Begins with the introduction சுருமன்னி வளர etc. Seems to record the promise of regular payment of paddy for the daily offerings throughout the year and for the requirement of the eiglt days of the festival in the month of Sittirai in the temple of Kalakaladēva, out of the land granted to the temple in the 18th year of the king, by Rajaraja-Mūvenda[vēlān].

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the south wall of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.date: 13th year, Kumbha, amāvāsya, Monday, Aviṭṭam, Kōṭṭu-nāḷ (?) 237. [date-calculation appendix, No. 242: 13th year, Kumbha, ba. amāvāsyā, Monday, Avittam, Koṭṭuṇai ? 237. Ba. amāvāsyā was current on Sunday, 30th January, A.D. 998. The week-day quoted in the inscription is perhaps a mistake. The tithi and the nakshatra were current on Sunday till ‘68 and ‘71 respectively.]
cells.remarks: Built in in the middle. Begins with the introduction of the king etc. Records the purchase of some lands belonging to the temple of Tiruvirāma-uḍaiya-Paramasvāmi, at the instance of the assembly (sabhā) of Kadavūr in Ambar-nāḍu in Uyyakkondār-vaḷanāḍu, by a certain Uḍaiyāndirān Ammāḻan alias [Kaḷakkāḍu]-Māyilaṭṭi a merchant residing in the village, who got it made rent-free by the assembly with the stipulation that he should pay a fixed quantity of paddy to the temple every year for the expenses of worship and for maintaining three lamps before certain images.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the east wall of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.king: Kulôttunga-Chôla I †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Begins with the introduction புகழ்ச்சி யோடு விளங்க etc., of Kulôttunga-Chôla I. Records a sale of 14 veli of land which had been lying fallow for fifty years without any cultivation, as tax-free appurtenance with the taxes remitted by ohâdimânniam, as bettered by the assembly (mahâsabhai) of Tirukkâdêvavur in Âmbur-nâdu in Râjarâjavaḷanâdu, to certain Vanavarāyar of Kopparamangalam in Pâmburik-kôram, a subdivision of Sûtramalli-vaḷanâdu, for feeding daily in the Markandéyan-madan tan Siuyôgis well-versared in the Vedas, for the welfare of the king. Mentions the Tiruchchiyarambala-Vêlaikkâran tirumanilapaṇ in the temple, as the place where the sabhā held its meeting.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the east and north walls of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction திருமாமழை பொழிய etc. Records a gift of some lands as Salabhôgam after bringing them under cultivation, by a certain Pôchchan Adittan alias Vijayarājēndra-Mûvênd-vôlaj of Kômukkuli to feed seventeen persons in the Râjâdirâjan-śalai and to feed the expenses of worship in the temple of Kālakaladêva.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the north wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction கடற்சூழந்த பாரமாதேவி etc. Records a gift of some land to the king to the temple of Tiruviraṇtapa-Nâkayar at Linkkôndaikkuḍi in Akkur-nâdu, a subdivision of J-yavigaṇdośja-rajanājan, confirming its possession of all the tax-free lands in and outside the village, and exempting them from the payment of a lump sum for the remission of taxes on the lands.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the west wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1443, Vikrama, Mithuna, ba. tritiyā, Friday, Tiruvōṇam. The cyclic year Vikrama fell in Śaka 1442 and the date intended was A.D. 1520, June 4, Monday ; ·24; f.d.n. ·05. The week-day quoted in the inscription is probably a mistake. [from date-calculation appendix, No. 246]
cells.language: Saka 1443, Vikramu, Mithuna, ba. tritiya, Friday, Tiruvōpam.
cells.remarks: Record a grant of 8 vēli of land and of some privileges in the temple of Kalakaladēvar in perpetuity to three persons named Āditta-Bhuiṭar Kariyamanikka-Bhatṭar, Pukkattaraivallasōla-Brahmarāyar and Kariyamanikka-Bhatṭar Āparshayūr who interviewed the king at Vijayanagara and got the jōdi and sūlavari on certain villages which had been remitted by the king already in favour of the temple but not given effect to, now ratified.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the west wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.language: Saka 1443, Vikramu, Mithuna, ba. tritiya, Friday, Tiruvōpam.
cells.remarks: Registers a tax-free gift by the king, at the request of Kalingarâyan, of 31 vēli of land at Kulottungasôja-Karappur separated from Akkur alias Râjêndrasinhachaturvêdimangalam for the expenses of the daily service and special worship on the Arra-sandhi after noon in the temple, and of special worship on the day of Mâla in the month of Âyi in which he was born.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.date: Saka 1307, Krodharu, Tulā, sū. Wedneeduy, pūrnai, Aśvati. [date-calculation appendix, No. 248: 27th year, Dhanus 16, Wednesday, Attam = A.D. 1096, December 10, Wednesday ; ·28. The tithi ashṭamī was current till ·17 on Wednesday.]
cells.language: Saka 1443, Vikramu, Mithuna, ba. tritiya, Friday, Tiruvōpam.
cells.remarks: Records a sarvamānya gift of all the money due to the king out of the various taxes on 100 vēli of land, for the maintenance of worship in the temple of Kalankaladēvar at Tirukkadaiyur, a brahmadeya in the eastern subdivision of Jayangondasôja-vaḷanâdu.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged and portions of lines 13 to 28 completely lost. Seems to be an exact copy of No. 245 above.

cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.date: 4th year, Mina, ba. saptami, Thurs-day, Mūla.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 3 wli of land free of taxes as archand-bhoga for the worship of the image of Tirukkadavūr-Nāyakar in the temple of Tillaiyāl-Īśvaramudaiyār at Tillaiyāl-nallūr in Kuṇrā-nādu, a subdivision of Kula-ttungachōla-valanādu. Mentions the ohanne called Arulakara-vāyakkāl.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr
cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged and stones lost. Similar to Nos. 167, 184, 228 and 235 above. Tirukkadavūr is mentioned last in the list of the villages benefitted by the king's remission of 10,000 varāhaṇ in favour of the Siva and Vishṇu temples of those places.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the west wall of the first pri-karu of the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the royal grant, at the request of Pallavarayar, of some lands to the south of the temple for houses and for flower-gardens and filled it with water for irrigation. Some wet-land channels at the village of Trukkaṭṭuchēri which had been endowed for the maintenance of the perpetual lamps, and to make the residents of Kávirippūmbuttam responsible for the safe oustody of the temple jewels and utensils.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the west wall of the first pri-karu of the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Begins with the introduction சண்ட சண்ட etc. Seems to record some agreement given by the mahāsabhā of Tirukkadavūr included in Ambar-nādu, a sub-division of Akkar-nādu to the 240 Periyamayūr (assembly of elders) of Ambar-nādu regarding the colleo-tion of rents from lands and the disposal of unclaimed property in the village.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr
cells.place: On the west wall of the first pri-karu of the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction புவன முடையார் etc. Records the grant of some public land for the maintenance of a gardener looking after the flower-garden made by the parigarakkaran Appan Ponnambalam in the temple of Kalakkadavērar at Tirukkadavūr in Akkar-nādu, a subdivision of Jayangondaśōla-vulanādu after par-ohasing its tax-free from the assembly of the village.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr
cells.place: On the west wall of the first pri-karu of the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the royal sanction to the confirmation of the ap-pointment of mettu-veenaṇ (dance master and musician) in the temple, together with its income in paddy, on certain Parudiyan/ ponnan alias Kalakkuṇdū-Ni[r*]kap-pērayan, at the request of Virarāpa-Pallavarayai an favourite poet of the king.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr
cells.place: On the west wall of the first pri-karu of the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Unfinished. Refers to a memorial submitted to the king by 240 Velims of Tirukkadavūr in Ambar-nādu.

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr †
cells.place: On the west wall of the first pri-karu of the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.date: 14th year, Bishubha, 6n. pañchamI, Tuesday, Pūṣam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 257: 14th year, Rishabha, śu. pañchami, Thursday, Pūśam = A.D. 1160, May 12, Thursday ; ·41; ·34.]
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction பூருவ தேசமும் etc. Records a decision of the mahāsabhā of Tirukkēdavar in Akkur-nāḍu, assembled in the Kulōttuṅgaśōḷan-tiruvēduttukkāḷi (hall) in the temple of Kaḷakāḷēśvara, who, contrary to the property of those Mahēśvaras who, contrary to their ten ts as the custodians of the Siva temple and its observances interin ingled freely with the Vaishnavas and sold the losses (grown for the god).

cells.location: Tirukkadaiyūr
cells.place: On the west wall of the first pri-karu of the Aruḷāḻēśvara temple. †
cells.date: 14th year, Paṅguṇi, ba. 13, Monday, Sadaiyam. [date-calculation appendix, No. 258: 14th year, paṅguni, ba. 18, Monday, Sādayam = A.D. 1160, March 7, Monday ; ·81; ·82. Tribhuvanachakravartin Rājādhirājadéva (II).]
cells.remarks: Begins with the introduction பூருவ தேசமும் etc. Records the tunisiam of taxes on ṉilam and at Rājarājanallūr, a hamlet of Kalakāḷēśvaram, belonging to the temple of Kalakāḷēśvara by the assembly of that village in return for a lump payment of 300 kaśu from the temple. Refers to a drought in Avaṇi and Purāṭṭāśi months and the consequent failure of crops.

cells.location: Tirumayam
cells.place: On the north wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Brahmapurīśvara temple
cells.date: [9]th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 259: 4th year, Mīna, ba. saptamī, Thursday, Mūla = A.D. 1122, March 2, Thursday ; ·68; f.d.n. ·47.]
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Records an order of the assembly of Muvaṇḍi alias Uttamaśōḷa-chaturvēdimangalam in Nāḍu, a subdivision of Rājarājarāja-nāḍu, remitting the taxes kaḍamai and kudimai on the lands at Komāra-Kulōttuṅga-chaturvēdimangalam in the temple of Tirumayam-Uḍaiyār at Tirumayam after obtaining them from the assembly and as kaṭṭalai from certain residents of the village by Palaiyanūruḍaiyār... in the 3rd year of Periyadēva.

cells.location: Tirumayam †
cells.place: On the west wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Brahmapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the remission of taxes by the assembly of Irukkadavar in Amūr-nāḍu, a subdivision of Akkur-nāḍu, on a land granted as tiṇṇamattakkāṇi to the temple of Tirumayamuḍaiya-Perumāḷ by a resident of the village.

cells.location: Tirumayam †
cells.place: On the south wall of the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine in the Brahmapurīśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged and stones out of order and some lost. Begins with the introduction பூருவ தேசமும் etc. Refers to the incidents of the war of Pandya succession in which the Cholas helped Kulachēkhara (to the Pāṇḍya throne) against the Ma-Pāṇḍya. Records a tax-free gift of land to a person (name lost) who distinguished himself in the campaign.

cells.location: Tiruvidaikkali
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Stones lost. Seems to record a gift of land for feeding two persons (in the temple) by a certain Sembiyan Koruperunka[iyur] of Kagr[r*]-nādu in Manayir-kōṭtam, a subdivision of Toṇdai-nādu.

cells.place: On the east wall of the first prākāru of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.remarks: Stones lost. Seems to record a gift of land to the feeding two Pillaiyar Tirukkuruvaidaiyar at [Tiruv]idaikkali by the assembly for opening a road to the sea for taking the image of the god for sea-bath on festival occasions. Mentions a survey made in the 16th year of Kulot-tunga-Chola[deva].

cells.location: Tiruvaidakkali †
cells.place: On the east wall of the first prākāru of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.date: Šuka 1377, Yuva, Tola, 6u. trayōdaśi, Friday, Bevati, Agpaśi 24.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 40 veli of land with all its income in the villages of Kilaryur and Andur included in Tiruvatar-nsavadi for the maintenance of a matha in charge of a pontiff (name lost), made by Saluva Tirumalaiyadeva Maharaja in the presence of the god Sri Sarangapadeva at Kumbhakonam.

cells.location: Tiruvidaikkali
cells.place: On the east wall of the first prākāru of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of the balance of produce on 5 vēli of land after running out the yield to the temple at 50 kalam on each vēli by a certain Perumballi-Kandan Su[ndara] out of his possessions as tenant of the temple lands, for feeding Brahmins in a matha called Tiruvā-rāmivartta-madam.

cells.location: Tiruvaidakkali †
cells.place: On the north wall of the first prākāru of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.date: 14th year, Rishabha, ba. shashthi, Saturday, Uttara-bha. jam.
cells.remarks: Records a provision made by the perumakkal (assembly) of Tiruvidaikkali, for the annual payment of 287 kalam and odd of paddy as tax, collected by the owners of several specified lands in the village, in return for the remission of taxes granted on those lands.

cells.location: Tiruvaidakkali †
cells.place: On the north wall of the first prākāru of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.date: 10th year, Simha, ba. trayōdaśi, Sunday, Punar-pūsam.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land as tirunāmattukkāni by the perumakka! of Tiruvidaikka[i] for the maintenance of worship to the image of Aiññārava-Vinayakappi[i]aiyar set up in the Śēnapatip-perunderavu (street) by a merchant, who had also made a similar gift of land for the same purpose.

cells.location: Tiruvaidakkali †
cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāru of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a tax-free grant of land at Tiruvidaikka[i] and some other villages by order of the king for the maintenance of a maṭha built by a certain Kappagānjeri-Nārayanan of the Tiruviramiśvaram-Pagavar. The royal secretary was Vanavaṇ-Mūvēn[davēlaṇ].

cells.location: Tiruvaidakkali †
cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāru of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a gift of 2 muli of land for a garden at Nalla dai-Mañgudi by Kōkkali-Peṇpumali-Nambi for a perpetual lamp and for worship to the image of Arulalap-Perumal set up in the Trukkadambī-madam by a certain Kok-kalliyankkaṇaiyan.

cells.location: Tiruvidaikkali
cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāru of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.remarks: Registers a gift by purchase of 5 vēli and odd of land in the haulet Podimangalam after getting the remission of its taxes from the assembly of Tiruvidaikhali, by a certain Kuprattu-Narayanaṇ, for the maintenance of Brabmin students of Pēdānta from the Malayalam country in the maṭha established by him at Tirukundai Śhaggiyatturai. Records also the presentation by the same donor of some women for hereditary service in the maṭha.

cells.location: Tiruvidaikkali
cells.place: On the south wall of the first prākāru of the Subrahmanya temple. †
cells.remarks: Records a sale of about 4 vēli of land as Rājurājaṇ-parseilni by order of the king, for 20750 kāśu, to a certain Sivadavanapperumāl of Pūvaṇṭr, who endowed the same to the temple for the maintenance of the early morning service called 'Manniyakkōt[u]-Mūttatāradun-Sandi'. Refers to some lands in Tribhuvanavira-obatury edimangalum presented as Sōdakumbha for the merit of 'Periyadevar' (Kulotturiga-Chola III †).

cells.location: Hansi
cells.place:
Kudligi taluk. Bellary district.
On astone set up in the Bamesvara temple
cells.date: Chalukya-Vikrama year 85, Vi[krita], Srāvaṇa, śu. 5, Monday.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers the grant of some land for worship, offerings, etc. in the temple of Paraśuramēsvara at Hanase situated near Kōgaji 500, by Mahasamsenta Ho[lle]ya while Tribhuvanamalla-[Pandya] was governing the Nogatabavadi, 32,000 country. The grant was made by the donor after washing the feet of his teacher Sōma[kartthara]-Pandita of the Kalamakha sect. The names of the composer and the engraver are given.

cells.location: Hansi †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Kaleśvara temple in the village. †
cells.remarks: Fragment. The inscription stops with the date.

cells.location: Bennakal
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Kaleśvara temple
cells.date: Śaka 1148, [Vyaya], Chaitra, Sura, Sunday, Uttarā-yaṇa-Samkrāmi, Vyatīpata.
cells.remarks: Extols the Hoysoļa dynasty and traces its descent from Sula. Sodanda-Dandanayaka, the Pradhane (chief Minister) Amityo-Dandanayaka of Hoysala King Pratapa-Kava-naraya, constructed the temples of Kamyēśvara, Ampritesvara, Lakshmi-Narayana, Vanōdēvara, Ballalēśvara and Narasimha at Bennakullu, the chief town of the sub-division Boppanahalli-Twelve situated in the Kōgali 500 province which formed part of the Noṇambavādi-nādu, and that he made grants of land in several villages for its worship, maintenance and repairs. The grants are said to have been made by him in the presence of the gods Vajrēśvara and Sōmanathevada after washing the feet of the (Saiva) teacher Kaléśvaradēva who is called here the Rājaguru (royal preceptor).

cells.location: Sovanahalli
cells.place: On the east face of the pedestal of the dhvajastambha in front of the Hanuman temple
cells.remarks: Records that a stone pillar was erected in the village of Sovanahalli by Māroja and Mallōja, the artisans of the Chōranaduru-śāsana.

cells.location: Sovanahalli †
cells.place: On the east face of the pedestal of the dhvajastambha in front of the Hanuman temple. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record the erection of the same pillar by Māroja of Horamale-śāsana (perhaps in conjunction with the donor of the above inscription).

cells.location: Sovanahalli †
cells.place: On the north face of the pedestal of the dhvajastambha in front of the Hanuman temple. †
cells.remarks: Records that Chaparanhalli and Appankunte were the villagers granted to Māroja as a hereditary gift for the duties of artisan.

cells.location: Sovanahalli †
cells.place: On the north face of the pedestal of the dhvajastambha in front of the Hanuman temple. †
cells.remarks: States that the temple of Basavavara (in the place) was built by Māroja and Mallōja.

cells.location: Sovanahalli †
cells.place: On a slab lying on the threshing floor known as Gīṭigaru-kannu at Gentikatte, hamlet of the village. †
cells.date: 22, Pramādi, Jyeshṭha, Puṇṇami, Tuesday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 285:  22, Pramādi, Jyēshṭha, Puṇṇami, Tuesday. cells.remarks: Records the death of hero named Saviga in a fight with the army of Śinga (?) which had laid siege to Moradakoṭe (fort).

cells.location: Sovanahalli †
cells.place: On a rock near a mosque on the way between Kalingere and Sovanahalli.
cells.remarks: Records that this field was a gift of Vāmarasa Amitayya-Daṇṇayaka.

cells.remarks: Records that a land at Iliribāju (where the inscription is found ?) was granted to god Svāmideva by Amitayya-Daṇṇayaka, Kēśava-Nāyaka-Sāvidēva, Hiriya-Sāvi-dēva and other officers.

cells.location: Choranur
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Hanuman temple
cells.remarks: Registers a proclamation issued by Immadi-Rāja-Nāyaka of Gudekōṭe and Sondūru to the people of Horamale-śīme by which he promised to deal with them as during the time of the Gudekōṭe rule.

cells.location: Choranur †
cells.place: On a slab built into the verandah of the Pīrāta-maṭha in the same village (as Hanuman temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers a cowl, granted by Bannoni-Nāyaka to the people of Horamale-śīme by the order of Rājādhirāja-Rājaparameśvara, the agent of Rājādhirāja-Rājaparameśvara, that in that part of the country no taxes would be levied on new born children (edagere) and dead bodies (mītene-āṇike).

cells.location: Choranur †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Vīrabhadrasvāmi temple in the same village (as Pīrāta-maṭha). †
cells.date: Śaka 14°9 (wrong), Sadharapa (Sadharapa fell in Śaka 1412 and 1472), Karttika, ba. 3
cells.remarks: Registers that they had made to the Vīrabhadrasvāmi temple, śēnabōvas, carpenters and blacksmiths of Chōṇamanūru by Bannaha-Kāvuta, the agent of Rājādhirāja-Rājaparameśvara. It also states that they had to pay a tax of three varahas a year.

cells.location: Choranur †
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of a ruined temple to the west of the village Ankanamanahalli.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a garuḍa-kambha to the god Tiraven-galanatha of Aṅkaṇamanahalli by Tīmmana, son of Yeroja, and of a pillar for lighting lamps (uṭṭamale-kambha) by Koṇḍayya, son of Tīmmana mentioned above.

cells.location: Choranur †
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Śiva temple at Tumbaraguḍḍi, hamlet of Yeryayanahalli.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of three kāsu a day as rāisa, out of the taxes received by certain Dēvarasa-Narasapa for lighting lamps before god Hanumanta at Tumbaraguḍḍi.

cells.location: Choranur †
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the Hanumantarāya temple in Tumbaraguḍḍi, hamlet of Yeryayanahalli. †
cells.remarks: Registers a similar gift by the same person for lighting lamps before god Hanumanta at Tumbaraguḍḍi.

cells.location: Kudiramāvu
cells.place: On a slab set up near the gate-way
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records the grant of the village Hire-Kudiraṇ made by a certain Chinnayaraja to Virapaksha-Vidyabbinava Śaṅkara-Bharati-Nyami.

cells.location: Jiganahalli
cells.place: On a slab set up in in front of the Hanuman temple
cells.remarks: Mutilated and damaged. Seems to register a grant of land at Jiguneha[!]i] by Dalavayi Bari[mi-Na]yaka.

cells.location: Jiganahalli †
cells.place: On a slab set up in a field to the south-west of Huralihalu.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record a grant to god Avubhaladēva.

cells.place: On a slab set up at the entrance of Molanūru, hamlet of Kenchamallanahalli.
cells.remarks: Records the setting up of a stone fixing the boundary of the village Molanūru after Mallana had performed (the ceremony of) walking over the boundary in the presence of some prominent men among whom was mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Ghaṇṭige[varu]śa.

cells.location: Jiganahalli †
cells.place: On a slab lying near the fresh-water well to the south-west of Katrikehatti, hamlet of Tippehalli.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a grant of land by Muda-Buuappa, son of Mudv-Virapa.

cells.location: Lokikere
cells.place: On a slab lying near the old tank
cells.remarks: Records that (this place where the stone was found ?) is the site of mahāgrāma Lokeyakere, the dear disciple of Śri Sadāśiva-Bhārati-Svāmi.

cells.place: On a slab lying under a banyan tree near the ruined village Dombarahalli, hamlet of Hosahalli. (On the way from Hosahalli to Horihalu).
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record the grant, of a village to Guramma of Yelamoduhu by Vimmadi-Nayakan.

cells.location: Jiganahalli
cells.place: On a slab set up in the temple of Basava
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register a grant of land to Virappayya son of Keśalavadēva.

cells.place: On a slab set up near the tankbund at Chikkakariyaginahalli.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of Rāmāṇuja[ya] who was appointed as the governor of Kondravīdu by Achyutadēvarāya. His several acts of charity are recorded, such as the building of a temple, construction of a tank, formation of agrahāras. Also records in particular the construction of a tank called Lakhasamudra for the merit of his mother.

cells.location: Ammamanakeri
cells.place: On a slab set up on a platform in the street
cells.remarks: The characters look like Vaṭṭeluttu.

cells.location: Huliganata
cells.place: On a stone built into the tank-bund
cells.date: Śaka 1478, Nila, Vaiśākha, śu. 3. [date-calculation appendix, No. 304: Śaka 1450, Sarvadhāri, Śrāvaṇa, śu. 15, Friday = A.D. 1528, July 31, Friday ; ·49.]
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the temple of god Bala-Krishna and the founding of the village Aohobutapura for the merit of his daughter Achchattamma, by Bayakara Rāmaṇpayya, and enumerates the same charities as in No. 302 made in Śaka 1461, Vikāri.

cells.location: Huliganata †
cells.place: On a broken pillar lying before the ruined temple of Vasanta-Mallihārjuna at Devalāpura, hamlet of Gajjapura.
cells.date: Śaka 147[8], Virodhikrit, Pushya, ha. 80, Monday; Ardhōdaya. [date-calculation appendix, No. 305: Śaka 147[8], Virdhikit, Pushya, ba. 30, Monday, Ardhōdaya = A.D. 1552, January 25, Monday. The nak. was 'Śrāvaṇa' which was current till ·41 of the day.]
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register the grant of a village in the Moraba-sthalu to the god Vasanta-Mallikārjuna by Rāmupa-Nayaka (son of Vōlur-Timmaya-Nayaka), who was the agent of Krishapa-Nāyaka, son of Bhairapa-Nāyaka.

cells.location: Huliganata †
cells.place: On the broken pillar lying before the ruined temple of Vasanta-Mallikārjuna at Devalāpura, hamlet of Gajjapura. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Registers the grant of a village to Mo[si]-ya-Kauta for the service of the god Vasanta-Malhkār-juna. It also registers a grant of Kādārambha-mānya to the goldsmith Śriyaṇa who engraved the inscription.

cells.location: Ujjini
cells.place: On a slab lying in the compound of the Siddhēśvara temple
cells.remarks: Praises Jagaddala-Paṇḍya of the Kadamba-kula and records the grant, made by him to god Kulidēva, of 400 kamtas of land at Kōgali. The engraver of the inscription was the goldsmith Kētoja, son of Basavaja.

cells.location: Ujjini †
cells.place: On a slab lying beside the central shrine of the Siddhēśvara temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1461, Vikri[ti], Bhādrapada, śu. 12, Tuesday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 308: Śaka 1461, Vikṛiti, Bhādrapada, śu. 12, Tuesday = A.D. 1539, August 26, Tuesday ; ·26. The nak. was 'Śrāvaṇa' which was current till ·72 of the day.]
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 'Ānanikanchi' made by the king to Brahmins.

cells.location: Ujjini †
cells.place: On a pillar in the maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine of the Siddhēśvara temple. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. The characters belong to the 18th Century A.D.

cells.location: Ujjini †
cells.place: On a broken slab planted in a field in the village. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of a land and two tamarind trees to a disciple of Liṅgakoṇḍeva made by Margasa[ya]- Nāyaka of Veluru for the merit of his father.

cells.location: Tulahalli
cells.place: On a slab lying in front of the temple of Basava
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the temple of Basavēśvara by Yayrapa-Nāyaka, son of Mahananayacharya Tammala-Nāyaka of Kaṇakuppe-durga.

cells.location: Tulahalli †
cells.place: On a broken Nāga-stone lying outside the village. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to record the setting up (of this Nagastone) by [Ku]mārakālī-Paṇḍita and mentions the sculptor Kētoja.

cells.location: Tulahalli †
cells.place: On a broken hero-stone lying outside the village. †
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Seems to record the victory of a hero.

cells.location: Tulahalli †
cells.place: On a slab set up-in front of the temple of Hanuman at Chinenehalli, hamlet of Kalapura.
cells.remarks: Records the rights of the gaudike and sēnabōnike of the village Sēshamanahalli (whose boundaries are given) belonged to Akuṇṇala Jaganatha-Śāstri of the Yajurveda and of the Mulikimallu, that taiyavārike to Beḍasa-Mariyappa of Madihalli and the rights of other (minor) offices to the family of Kaṭṭamane of Vujjini.

cells.location: Tulahalli †
cells.place: On a slab set up in front of the temple of Hanumān at Halyam.

cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the dynasty from Taila down to Vikramāditya (VI). It also registers grants of land made by several other people.

cells.location: Kottur
cells.place: On a slab built into the front wall of the Karnam's house
cells.remarks: Records the remission of taxes payable by the barbers, granted by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Aḷiya Rāmarājadēva at the request of the barbers Timmōja, Koṇḍōja and Bhadrōja.

cells.location: Kottur †
cells.place: On another stone near the front wall of the Karnam's house, temple of Hanumān. †
cells.remarks: Registers the remission of taxes (on sheep due from) the shepherds of Koṭṭūru-sīme, a subdivision of Kōgaḷiya-vēnṭhe in the Hastināvati-vaḷita, granted in the presence of the god Kālinātha at Bāgaḷi by a Nāyaka (name lost) bearing the title 'Mahānāyakāchārya', for the merit of his parents.

cells.location: Kottur †
cells.place: On a stone planted before the ruined Kallēśvara temple in the village. †
cells.date: Chalukya-Vikrama year 56, Nandana, Vaiśakha, śu. 3, Thursday, Uttarāyaṇa-Sunkrānti.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of some lands and house-sites made by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Ghaṭṭiyarasa of the Kadamba lineage who was governing Kōgaḷi 500, while Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Tribhuvanamalla-Pāṇḍyadēva was ruling over Nonambavāḍi 32000, for worship and offerings to the god Mūlasthāna-Rāmēśvara of Koṭṭūru. The grant was made into the hands of the Āchārya of the temple, Amṛitarāśi-Paṇḍita after washing his feet.

cells.place: On a stone set up in front of the Mūrukal-maṭha in the same village.
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of land made in commemoration of their success in a battle, by Bembidēva and Kēśava-Daṇḍanāyaka to Śaṅkaranārāyaṇa-Bhaṭṭa and others, with the permission of Sōyidēva-Ghaṭṭidēva, son of Jagadaḷa-Bammidēva.

cells.location: Maraba

cells.remarks: Similar to No. 303 above.

cells.place:

cells.place: On a slab set up in the compound of the Hanumān temple
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of lands made by Siṁgayya-Heggaḍe, son of Vārṇarasa and the chief of Chamdeyamangala to the temple of Mallikārjuna, Bhairava and Kannēśvara which were built by him in the village during the governorship of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Tribhuvanamalla Bhōgadēva-Chōḷa-Mahārāja.

cells.location: Rakaṭla

cells.remarks: Fragment. Ende abruptly after giving the date.

cells.remarks: Records the construction of the temple of Rāmēśvara, set Rakatu and the grant of some land for worship therein after washing the feet of Saṁgarāti.

cells.location: Rakaṭla †
cells.place:
On a slab lying in a field about 3

cells.remarks: Registers the grant of some land to Bhaira-Vadeya, son of Liṅganṇa-Vadeya by Rājarāi-Śēshabhūshanda for the merit of the Raja of Golkonda.

cells.location: Rakaṭla †
cells.place:
On a slab lying in a field about 1½
miles from Mailavrampalle.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Records the gift of some land to the god Kāmaśvara by two private individuals of Kavu kuṇṭe.

cells.location: Rakaṭla †
cells.place: On a slab planted in front of the temple of Hanumān at Hanamasala.

cells.place: On another slab planted in front of the temple of Hanumān at Hanamasala. †
cells.remarks: Records certain concessions shown to the villagers of Hanamasala as the village was going to ruins and the consequent arrangement made by Sōmaya-Nāyaka, the agent of Chaparada-Nāyaka about the shares of the produce of the lands that were to be paid to the palace and those to be reserved by the tenants.

cells.location: Rakaṭla †
cells.place:
On the walls round the Aṇaikalta-Perumal temple at Kaḷaippal,
Ṭhiruttaraippundī 'āluk, Tanjore district.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a sale of 565 mā of land for 1,500 paṇam by a number of persons residing at Mudivaṭaṅguśola-chaturvēdimangalam, a brahmadēya in l'uṭ-ṅgarambai-naḍu a sub-division of Rajendraśola-valanaḍu. to a certain Śokka-Nāyaṇar l'arakrama-Pandya-Malavarayar.

cells.place: On a slab lying in the Aṇaikalta-Perumal temple at Kaḷaippal, Ṭhiruttaraippundī 'āluk, Tanjore district. †
cells.remarks: States that the land called Kurichohimulai with its boundaries (lost) defined, belongs to Ānaikatta-Peruma] at Kalappal.

cells.place: On the west wall of the Alaġiyanathasvāmi temple in the same village (as Aṇaikalta-Perumal temple). †
cells.remarks: Reports the sale by the assembly (kūṭṭupropper umakkal) of Sūtzuvallinallur Sōpaṇkanallur, of land belonging to a certain Atiśarayan Mahādēva-Bhaṭṭar who had emigrated to the Pāṇḍya country where he died subsequently without paying the taxes due on his property from the 18th year of Rājakēsarinarman alias Rājarājadēva.

cells.place: On the south wall of the Alaġiya-nathasvāmi temple in the village. †

cells.location: Pāttukōṭṭai, Pāttukōṭṭai taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the north wall of the ruined maṇḍapa in the Chandrasekhara-svāmin temple. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the sikkara and the construction of two maṇḍapas in the temple by a certain merchant called Tiruvēṅkaṭa-Seṭṭiyār.

cells.location: Pāttukōṭṭai, Pāttukōṭṭai taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On a stone preserved in the Taluk office in the village. †
cells.remarks: Proclaims that the inhabitants of the surrounding districts by Vavaḍi-Bavaḍi-Paṇḍitar-Ayyan, agent of Gēṇigēdhara-Paṇḍitar-Ayyan the king's agent, and a his final settlement at Paṭṭukōṭṭai after building a stone fortress.

cells.location: Pāttukōṭṭai, Pāttukōṭṭai taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On stones built into the walls of the fort in the village. †
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Seems to register a gift of land for worship in the temple [last lost]. Seems to mention Sellarkkas Paṇḍiyani-menkon [ḍa-śōla-caturvēdimangalam] as situated in Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.location: Kiliavaram, Nannilam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: On the well of Adipurīśvara †

cells.location: Kiliavaram, Nannilam taluk, Tanjore district † — Tamil Nadu
